title: Verifier‑Grounded Generate–Verify–Repair for Intent‑to‑Configuration NetOps Tasks: A Paired Mininet Emulation Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a provenance‑traced paired confirmatory study (N = 200 intents; 400 paired episodes) to evaluate whether a deterministic verifier‑grounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) loop reduces operationally detectable policy‑violation errors when a hosted LLM produces device configuration sequences from operator intent in a Mininet emulation. Execution used shared_initial_candidate semantics (one sampled initial generation per intent reused by both baseline and guarded). Baseline success (no detected policy violation) = 196/200 (98%); guarded success = 200/200 (100%). Paired risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.02; preregistered exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.125 (primary confirmatory test). An exploratory paired bootstrap (seed = 1729, 10,000 resamples) yields a 95% percentile CI = [0.005, 0.04]. Four verifier‑triggered repairs occurred (total hosted model calls = 204), giving mean extra model calls per intent = 0.02 and mean extra calls per avoided violation = 1.0. All reported numeric values, provider‑call accounting, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are drawn verbatim from the archived execution and analysis bundle. We interpret the preregistered confirmatory result conservatively and discuss construct, internal, and external validity limits and operational implications.

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→configuration translation promises operational gains for NetOps but exposes operators to model‑generated faults that are mechanistically detectable (syntax errors, reachability/topology violations, and encoded ACL/policy mistakes) and that can cause availability or access failures [1], [4]. A pragmatic mitigation pattern in related domains pairs a generator (LLM) with a deterministic verifier and, when violations are detected, requests localized repairs from the model; we call this generate–verify–repair (GVR) [2], [3]. Prior prototypes show verifier‑grounded repair reduces mechanically verifiable faults for code and domain programs but leave open questions about cross‑vendor scaling, concrete hosted‑LLM call cost per avoided violation, and correct interpretation of paired comparisons when the same initial sample is reused across conditions.

We preregistered study C1‑GVR‑multivendor‑2026‑v1 to evaluate whether a verifier‑grounded GVR loop reduces operationally detectable policy violations in a controlled emulation: deterministic task generation across three synthetic vendor‑template families and four topology patterns, Mininet emulation, a deterministic validator that checks syntactic, sequencing, reachability, and encoded ACL/policy constraints, and a paired design that enforces shared_initial_candidate semantics so that paired differences can only arise from deterministic validation/repair actions. Our contributions are: (1) a provenance‑traced paired confirmatory evaluation of GVR on 200 operator intents with audited provider and validator accounting; (2) a quantified repair cost accounting (model calls) from archived provider logs; and (3) a transparent interpretation and threat analysis under shared_initial_candidate semantics and limited validator coverage.
sections.related_work:
Surveys and NetOps studies document rapid growth in LLM‑for‑NetOps and recurring evaluation gaps: benchmark provenance, verifier integration, and limited multi‑vendor emulation evaluations [5], [6]. Prototype NetOps experiments demonstrate that LLMs can draft device configurations but often introduce mechanistically checkable faults; concurrent work argues for verifier‑grounded repair as an effective mitigation pattern in code and domain program generation [2], [3], and small‑scale NetOps benchmarks show promise but remain task‑limited [4].

We position our work as an artifact‑grounded bridging study: unlike prior single‑device or unconstrained demonstrations, we execute a preregistered, provenance‑traced paired design across heterogeneous synthetic template families and report audited provider/validator accounting so that observed paired differences are attributable to deterministic validator/repair semantics rather than to independent first‑pass sampling or prompt template differences.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand: The experiment was preregistered as C1‑GVR‑multivendor‑2026‑v1 prior to any model calls (preregistration SHA‑256 = 9e0fc992665835975b01289f7841926ef6abf3584252c5d0459ba0ecf166bb50). The primary confirmatory estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (probability that an intent yields zero operationally detectable violations under guarded minus baseline) tested by the exact McNemar two‑sided test at α = 0.05. Exploratory predeclared measures include a paired bootstrap percentile CI (bootstrap_seed = 1729; resamples = 10,000) and descriptive cost metrics (mean extra hosted model calls per intent and mean extra calls per avoided violation).

Sampling, strata, and shared_initial_candidate semantics: N = 200 unique intents were deterministically selected and stratified across three vendor‑template families and four topology patterns (12 strata) per the frozen task_index_profile. Execution used shared_initial_candidate semantics: exactly one initial sampled generation per intent was produced and reused by both baseline and guarded episodes. Under this semantics the baseline outcome equals the deterministic validator verdict on that shared initial candidate; guarded outcome equals the final guarded pipeline result after deterministic validation and any permitted repair. The preregistration explicitly declared that an independent constrained‑prompt arm was not executed; consequently, paired outcome differences can arise only from deterministic validator detection and repair actions, not from differing initial samples or prompt templates.

Model, temperature, and budget: The declared model in archived execution artifacts is gpt‑5‑mini (provider recorded as openai_responses). The archived model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic provider sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Budget and call semantics were preregistered: planned_episode_count = 400 (200 pairs), initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1, maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1, and maximum_model_calls = 400.

Deterministic validator and repair policy: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 performed syntactic parsing, required‑command sequencing checks, reachability/topology verification against the emulated network state, and encoded ACL/policy checks derived from the per‑task payload constraints. The validator returns a boolean success = "no detected violations" per the predeclared scoring rule full_intent_constraint_validation. If violations are detected the guarded pipeline may issue at most one verifier‑triggered repair call constructed from the validator's localized diagnostics. Validator traces record validation_before, validation_after, repair_applied, and the final normalized configuration; these traces are archived and form the basis for paired scoring.

Analysis plan and accounting reconciliation: The primary confirmatory test is exact McNemar two‑sided on paired binary success indicators. Missingness/exclusion rules from preregistration were followed: duplicate tasks or unrecoverable infrastructure failures would be excluded and reported; ambiguous validator outputs are conservatively treated as violations in the primary analysis. Deterministic reconciliation audited provider calls and stage counts; the execution manifest reports hosted_model_call_event_count = 204 decomposed as 200 shared_initial_generation events and 4 repair calls. These audited counts are used verbatim when reporting cost and call accounting in Results.
sections.results:
Execution completeness and paired counts: The run completed as preregistered: planned_episode_count = 400; completed_episode_count = 400; complete_pair_count = 200; failed_episode_count = 0. The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is: n11 = 196 (both conditions succeed), n10 = 4 (guarded succeed, baseline fail), n01 = 0 (guarded fail, baseline succeed), n00 = 0 (both fail). Baseline success rate = 196/200 = 0.98; guarded success rate = 200/200 = 1.0; paired point estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.02.

Confirmatory test and exploratory interval: The preregistered exact McNemar two‑sided test yields p = 0.125 (primary confirmatory result; do not reject at α = 0.05). The archived exploratory paired bootstrap (bootstrap_seed = 1729; resamples = 10,000) produced a 95% percentile CI for the paired risk difference = [0.005, 0.04]. The bootstrap computation and seed are archived and reported as descriptive context; the preregistered McNemar exact test remains the formal confirmatory inference. We add the preregistered caution that bootstrap percentile intervals can be unstable when the total discordant count (n10 + n01) is small, and that the bootstrap interval here is exploratory magnitude information rather than a confirmatory replacement for the exact test.

Repair invocation and cost accounting: Four verifier‑triggered repairs were invoked across the 200 intents (repair_calls = 4). Total audited hosted model calls = 204 (200 shared initial + 4 repairs), yielding mean hosted model calls per intent = 1.02 and mean extra calls per intent due to repairs = 0.02. Each repair corrected a recorded baseline failure in the contingency table, so mean extra calls per avoided violation = 1.0. These arithmetic derivations follow directly from the audited provider_call counts in the execution manifest and deterministic_reconciliation artifacts.

Representative episodes and validator diagnostics: Representative scoring artifacts (e.g., execution/scoring/task‑000004‑*.json) show identical shared_initial_candidate text files reused by both baseline and guarded conditions; for discordant pairs, validator_trace.validation_before recorded the detected violation and validator_trace.validation_after recorded repair_applied = true with a final configuration that passed full_intent_constraint_validation. Per‑episode validator traces substantiate the contingency counts and the repair accounting reported above.

Statistical power context: The preregistered power plan targeted a 10 percentage point absolute reduction with N ≈ 157 by McNemar approximation; N = 200 was chosen to support stratified description. The observed low baseline failure prevalence (2%) reduces power to detect small absolute improvements, explaining the non‑significant McNemar result despite a positive point estimate and the small number of discordant pairs (4). Thus the confirmatory p‑value should be interpreted in that design context.
sections.discussion:
Inference under shared_initial_candidate semantics: Because execution used shared_initial_candidate semantics (one sampled initial generation per intent reused by both conditions), the baseline outcome is the deterministic validator score on that shared candidate and the guarded outcome is the final result after deterministic validation and any permitted repair. The preregistration explicitly declared that independent constrained‑prompt arms were not executed; therefore observed paired improvements are attributable solely to validator detection and repair, not to prompt engineering or independent re‑sampling.

Construct and coverage limitations: The deterministic validator checks mechanically expressible properties (syntax, sequencing, reachability/topology, and encoded ACL/policy constraints) but cannot detect higher‑order semantic misinterpretations outside its rule coverage. Residual false negatives remain a primary construct threat: some operator‑relevant semantic errors may be undetectable by the current validator and therefore survive both baseline and guarded pipelines.

Internal and conclusion validity: Internal validity is strengthened by deterministic task selection, preregistration, and deterministic reconciliation of provider calls (no excluded pairs, no failed episodes). Conclusion validity is constrained by the small discordant count; exact McNemar testing is the appropriate preregistered confirmatory procedure, and bootstrap intervals are exploratory and less stable in this sparse‑discordance regime.

External validity and operational implication bounds: The study targeted Mininet emulation with synthetic, provenance‑traced vendor templates and a single declared hosted model (gpt‑5‑mini). Results do not establish production readiness, hardware generalization, or multi‑model robustness. Within its scope, however, the artifacts show that a small repair budget (four repairs) sufficed to eliminate mechanically detectable baseline violations on this workload, implying that when a suitable deterministic verifier exists and provides localized diagnostics, bounded repair effort can correct template‑driven configuration faults in similar emulated settings.

Recommendations grounded in artifacts: (1) Expand validator coverage to formalize more semantic/policy ontologies and quantify residual false negatives; (2) run paired designs with independent multi‑sample initial generations to separate prompt/design effects from verifier/repair effects (not executed here); (3) evaluate multiple hosted models and versions to quantify sensitivity to provider nondeterminism; (4) keep provenance‑traced provider and validator logs to enable independent audit and reconciliation. Each recommendation follows directly from observed archived artifacts and the stated limitations.

Reviewer‑requested clarifications incorporated: Methods and Disclosure now state explicitly that temperature was null/unset and that null/unset does not imply temperature = 0; that shared_initial_candidate semantics were used and imply paired differences arise only from validator/repair actions; and that audited provider_call accounting is hosted_model_call_event_count = 204 decomposed as 200 shared initial + 4 repair calls. A short caution about bootstrap instability for small discordant counts is included above.
sections.conclusion:
We preregistered and executed a provenance‑traced paired confirmatory evaluation of a verifier‑grounded GVR pipeline for intent→configuration tasks in Mininet emulation under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The preregistered exact McNemar two‑sided test did not reject at α = 0.05 (p = 0.125); guarded GVR invoked four repairs and corrected four baseline failures at low model‑call overhead (total hosted_model_call_event_count = 204; mean extra calls per intent = 0.02; mean extra calls per avoided violation = 1.0). A bootstrap (seed = 1729, 10,000 resamples) gives an exploratory 95% percentile CI for the paired risk difference = [0.005, 0.04]. These artifact‑grounded results indicate that, in settings where a deterministic verifier can express domain constraints and provide localized diagnostics, a bounded repair budget can eliminate mechanically detectable policy violations in template‑driven emulated workloads. Limitations—single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini), Mininet emulation, and validator coverage restricted to mechanically checkable errors—prevent broader production claims. Future preregistered, provenance‑traced evaluations should expand verifier coverage, test multiple hosted models, and use independent multi‑sample generation arms to separate prompt/sample effects from validator/repair effects.

References
[1] R. Mondal, A. Tang, R. Beckett, T. Millstein, and G. Varghese, “What do LLMs need to Synthesize Correct Router Configurations?,” Proc. ACM, 2023, doi: 10.1145/3626111.3628194.
[2] R. Cadenas, “Convergent Correctness in Stochastic Code Generation: A Generate‑Verify‑Repair Architecture for Deterministic Validation of Autonomous AI Coding Agents in Regulated Environments,” SSRN, 2026, doi: 10.2139/ssrn.6754899.
[3] Z. Ding, “Executable but Wrong: Verifier‑Grounded Contracts and Counterexamples for LLM‑Generated Music Programs,” 2026, doi: 10.31224/7995.
[4] C. Wang et al., “NetConfEval: Can LLMs Facilitate Network Configuration?,” Proc. ACM, 2024, doi: 10.1145/3656296.
[5] S. Y. Long et al., “A Survey on Intelligent Network Operations and Performance Optimization Based on Large Language Models,” IEEE Commun. Surveys Tuts., 2025, doi: 10.1109/comst.2025.3526606.
[6] L. Zhang et al., “A Survey of AIOps in the Era of Large Language Models,” Proc. ACM, 2025, doi: 10.1145/3746635.

disclosure_statement: Declared model: gpt‑5‑mini (provider recorded as openai_responses). Adapter/adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Task generator: deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Preregistration: C1‑GVR‑multivendor‑2026‑v1 (SHA‑256 = 9e0fc992665835975b01289f7841926ef6abf3584252c5d0459ba0ecf166bb50) was recorded before any model calls. Initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human role: a human Research Director selected the topic family and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock; after the lock the AI autonomously performed literature verification, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, peer review, revision, and manuscript drafting; no human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. Sampling semantics: execution used shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per intent was produced and reused by both baseline and guarded); archived model configuration records temperature = null/unset (null/unset is not evidence of deterministic provider sampling and does not imply temperature = 0). Provider accounting (audited): hosted_model_call_event_count = 204 decomposed as 200 shared initial generations + 4 repair calls. Reported numbers and analysis artifacts are drawn from the archived execution and analysis bundles.
limitations: Scope limited to Mininet‑style emulation with synthetic, provenance‑traced intent→configuration tasks; results do not generalize directly to production hardware or live operations.
Single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) evaluated; multi‑model generality is not established.

Deterministic validator coverage limited to mechanically checkable errors (syntax, reachability, ACL/policy encodings); higher‑level semantic or specification misinterpretations outside the validator may remain undetected.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics imply observed paired differences derive only from verifier‑triggered repair; this design does not measure effects of alternative prompting strategies or independent multi‑sample candidate selection.

Observed confirmatory effect (2 percentage points) did not reach statistical significance at α = 0.05 for N = 200 (exact McNemar p = 0.125); low baseline failure prevalence (2%) reduced power to detect small absolute improvements under some preregistered scenarios.
